tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Use for: loading a web page in a real Chromium browser and reading it. Returns the page title, final URL and a clean text extract (up to 8000 chars). Don't use when: you only need raw HTML or an API response — a plain HTTP fetch is cheaper. Errors are structured: NAV_TIMEOUT, NAV_FAILED, INVALID_URL

tools.name: browser_extract
tools.description: Use for: pulling repeated elements (prices, titles, links) from the page a session is on, via a CSS selector, or the full page text when no selector is given. Returns one string per matched element. Don't use when: the page has not been loaded yet — call browser_navigate first. Paid: $0.005 per call

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Use for: understanding page structure cheaply and deterministically — returns the accessibility tree (roles, names, states) as compact YAML instead of pixels or raw HTML. This is the lowest-token way to decide what to click or fill next. Don't use when: you need visual layout or images — use browser

tools.name: browser_act
tools.description: Use for: interacting with the page — click, fill, type, select, submit, press. Returns the resulting page title, URL and text so you can verify the action landed. Don't use when: the target element is not on the current page — navigate or snapshot first. This tool can change remote state (it can sub

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: Use for: visual verification — layout, images, charts, CAPTCHA presence, or evidence of page state. Returns a PNG image (JPEG if the PNG exceeds 2.5MB). Don't use when: you only need the page's content or structure — browser_extract and browser_snapshot are far cheaper in tokens. Paid: $0.02 per cal

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Use for: ending a session and freeing its browser. Sessions also expire automatically after 10 idle minutes. Free on every door — closing is never charged. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: browser_navigate · Private data: browser_snapshot, browser_screenshot · Public sink: browser_act.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: browser_navigate · Private data: browser_snapshot, browser_screenshot · Public sink: browser_act

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.detail: Tool "browser_navigate" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
